description: ZeroG Flames is an SI-powered web dashboard designed to combine all the combustion datasets & make NASA’s integrated microgravity combustion data instantly accessible  for professors, students, aerospace researchers& engineers.
summary:
When humanity travels to the Moon and Mars, the greatest threat isn't just the vacuum of space—it's fire. While NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database holds decades of vital combustion research, that massive volume of data can be overwhelming to navigate and apply.      

To solve this, we developed the ZeroG Flames Dashboard, an AI-powered platform that transforms raw microgravity combustion data into actionable intelligence. We built a custom Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline using Gemini 3.8-flash that directly ingests complex PSI research PDFs—like SAFFIRE and BASS—and presents insights through a highly intuitive interface.

ZeroG Flames directly addresses the challenge by evaluating fire scenarios across dynamic environments (ISS, Lunar, or Martian). It doesn't just summarize; it generates a relatability leaderboard that ranks the most relevant NASA investigations, provides match percentages, and links directly to official PSI repositories. It even highlights how this research improves terrestrial firefighter tech.

Fire behaves fundamentally differently in space, burning spherically without buoyancy. As we design next-generation habitats with elevated oxygen levels, understanding these dynamics is a matter of life and death. ZeroG Flames ensures critical safety data is instantly accessible, keeping our crews safe as we take the next giant leap.
details:
1. Overview: ZeroG Flames is an AI flight director for spacecraft fire safety. We built a RAG pipeline that ingests NASA PSI research. Users ask questions, and the AI retrieves physics-accurate data tailored to specific gravity environments (ISS, Lunar, Mars).
2. Benefits: It transforms overwhelming PDF archives into instant, actionable intelligence. It prevents AI hallucinations by grounding every answer exclusively in verifiable NASA experiments.
3. Impacts: It helps engineers design safer habitats for deep space, while accelerating the translation of microgravity research into better firefighter gear, smoke detectors, and extinguishers here on Earth.
4. Tools used: React, Tailwind CSS, Chart.js (Frontend); Python, FastAPI (Backend); Gemini 3.8-flash & 3.5 flash lite, LangChain, PyPDF2, ChromaDB (AI & Data).
5. Creativity: We created a closed-loop dashboard. Our code actively parses the AI's output to generate a visually animated "Relatability Leaderboard," automatically matching shorthand names to custom dictionaries to link directly to official NASA PSI source documents.
6. Factors considered: We prioritized strict zero-G physics accuracy (handling spherical flames and zero buoyancy) and engineered a high-stress, dark-mode UI with live data telemetry for professional aerospace use.
